The prototype at **http://maker:4001** now supports working with many links at once. Please try this sequence:

**1 — Select a few.** Each card now has a small circle on its left. Tap the circles on two or three cards. A dark **action bar** appears showing how many you've selected.

**2 — Select everything at once.** In that bar, click **"Select all N in this view."** This selects *every* link matching your current search and view — so an action can hit them all, not just what's on screen. *(This becomes especially handy once you can limit how many show at a time.)*

**3 — Change them together.** With several selected, try **Mark read**, then **Mark unread**. Then try **Add label** (type e.g. `triage` and Add) and **Remove label** — all applied to the whole selection at once.

**4 — Archive vs. Finished.** Select a couple and click **Archive**. Notice they leave your main list entirely — and if you search for them, they won't appear. Now click **Archived** (top-right). There they are, with the whole view flagged as hidden-from-normal. Click **Restore** on one to bring it back, then **← Back to list**.

**5 — Delete for good.** Select one and click **Delete**. It asks you to confirm a permanent removal before anything is lost.

Decisions I made that I'd like you to judge:
- **Archive** removes links from the list *and* search, keeping them only in the **Archived** view — clearly distinct from **Finished** (which stays in your list). Is that the separation you meant?
- **After a bulk action, the selection clears** so you start fresh. And **switching to Archived clears your current selection**. Do those feel right?
- **"Select all in this view"** means all results of the current search/view. Is that the scope you'd expect for "apply to every result"?
